newsitem.title: UK: Bass, F.Leisure no takeover comment.
newsitem.headline: Bass, F.Leisure no takeover comment.

text.p: Brewer-to-leisure group Bass Plc refused to comment on a report in the Sunday Times newspaper that it was looking to launch a 650 million stg takeover bid for First Leisure Corp Plc.
"We never comment on speculation," said a company spokeswoman. A spokesman for First Leisure said, "it is company policy that we do not comment on market rumour or speculation."

But analysts said Bass' advisers Schroders has expanded the list of potential targets to include First Leisure after the government blocked the group's 205 million plan to buy brewery group Carlsberg-Tetley in June.
Stockmarket rumours have continued to tie Bass with bookmaker Ladbroke Group Plc, betting chain William Hill owned by Brent Walker Group Plc and Stakis Plc, as well as European hotels.

Analysts said First Leisure has become a more attractive candidate given its recent share price underperformance and the greater likelihood venture capital firm CinVen will win the bidding race for William Hill.
"First Leisure would be an opportune deal, it is not a must-do type of acquisition. William Hill is a much more obvious fit," said one analyst who chose not to be named.

First Leisure shares have suffered since Michael Grade took over in June. They reached 376p once news of his arrival from Channel Four was first announced but had sunk to a year low of 292 pence by August.
Rumours that Bass may launch a bid for the group have since helped take the shares to 325p.

On June 24 the group disappointed the marketplace with a five percent decline in pre-tax profits to 17.2 million stg for the first six months of the year. It also warned that early second half trading had failed to meet expectations.
Its bingo hall division saw comparable sales in the first half fall 25 percent due to falling attendance and reported a loss of 1.3 million stg.
